brief: BTIG's technical strategy note argues October is historically a bullish reversal month (2002, 2011, 2022), but those reversals followed drawdowns of about 48%, 22%, and 27%, while the SPX is currently about flat since June and near all-time highs, which weakens the seasonal analog. Despite 9 of 11 sectors falling more than 2% over the last month, equity and composite put/call ratios are near the year's lows and the VIX Daily Sentiment Index is just 19%, which the note reads as complacent positioning, making the risk of a higher-correlation volatility event high for October. Separately, 30-year yields rose from 5.25% to 5.69% in 7 sessions with bond Daily Sentiment at 10%, which the note treats as tactical upside exhaustion and a risk of a snap-back lower in yields. If yields fall, the note expects the QQQ vs IWM ratio to reverse, so breadth could rebound even as QQQ and Mag7 move lower. RSP's tactical risk/reward is no longer negative as it nears its 200-day moving average, versus greater downside risk the note sees in SPY, QQQ and Mag7. B vs CCC credit spreads are also at fresh wides, through 7%.
